newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks open weak, retail confidence limp.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks open weak, retail confidence limp.

text.p: Singapore shares languished in thin mid-morning trade on Tuesday as continued selling by institutions and foreign funds dampened retail confidence, dealers said.
"There is continued liquidation in the domestic market, more in Malaysia and that is affecting the retail confidence," said a broker with a local house.
He said institutions remained net sellers, trimming their positions with the U.S. market promising better returns.
At 0230 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 3.13 points at 1,999.92. Turnover was around 25 million with 124 losers to 57 gainers.
Malaysian KLI Holdings, which topped the actives with over 3.6 million shares, continued to suffer from forced selling after the Bank of Negara tightened loans on shares trading.
Shares in the property and consumer products firm hit a new year low at S$1.73 against a high of S$2.99 on March 13.
Singapore Telecommunications Ltd also hit a new low of S$2.35 amid tough competition in Singapore. City Developments continued to reel from fears of more government curbs on the property market.
The property index fell 10.67 points to a new low at 646.37.
